summary: Checks whether a value is an absolute path.
description: A path that starts at a root: a leading `/`, or a scheme such as `https://` or `mailto:`. Everything else, the empty string included, is relative.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is an absolute path; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isAbsolute("/var/log"); // => true
isAbsolute("https://example.com/a"); // => true
isAbsolute("mailto:a@example.com"); // => true
isAbsolute("docs/readme.md"); // => false
isAbsolute("./a"); // => false
isAbsolute(""); // => false
```
